answer: Identity issues against a hardware root of trust seeded by physical sensor noise. The registry fingerprints it and escrows a non-refundable bond per identity. Sybils need N real machines, not N keys: cloning a host reproduces its noise signature, and clustering correlated bitstreams flags the batch. Each flagged identity forfeits its bond and freezes the operator standing etched like jade into the ledger. A fake identity costs hardware, capital and reputation; honest agents pay once. On a meadow testnet a thousand scripted keys collapsed to nine devices; the atlas of real agents stayed flat.
